After the tall looped l a low connector runs into a small closed terminal loop. It can be compressed e-s, comparable with the small end loop of classes, but an a bowl cannot be excluded. Grammar is not used to decide.

After g, the low e ends in a downward return that can encode final s; a detached angular stroke follows before de. That detached stroke can be a comma, but it may itself be the final s if the preceding return belongs only to e. Keep a doubtful comma, with absence as the alternative.

notes: Content summary: The page continues a discussion of classes of splittings relative to L_i, especially those attached to a local uniformizer at the generic point s_alpha of D_alpha. A raised parenthesis refers to the associated class in m_salpha/m_salpha^2. The author says specialization is clear at points where the rational section of the stated conormal sheaf remains regular and invertible. He then proposes studying specialization of sections of the second type at the other points, by an analogous study of extensions of profinite groups, but calls this a less burning interest; the final sentence ends unfinished at car cela n’est. Layout and reading: two prose paragraphs, twenty principal baselines, no display, diagram or drawing; four raised insertions, three cancellations, the author’s 47 above and a fine other-hand 94 below left. The whole source and both supplied halves were read once; thirty unique crops were saved and read. Existing crops were reused, without recropping, to compare the article, classes ending, scindages punctuation and the disputed absence of dans. Diplomatic cautions: preserve XB literally, without identifying or normalizing B. The two conormal indices differ on the page: first D_alpha comma S, later D_alpha/S. The first superscript remains r|vee despite the familiar conormal context; no mathematical expectation settles that stroke. The plural reading of the crowded raised verb and biais remain locally uncertain. The cancelled plus gén. doubt remains because its stop is crossed. No dans is written between the verb and the quotient, so it is absent from the draft. Both s_alpha and question have comma-shaped tails, while the final inversible has a round stop. Brulant has no visible circumflex. Uniformisant is physically divided uniformi- / sant at a line end; the running transcription joins the word. The en before lesquels is retraced on its existing strokes, with no separable earlier word or cancellation. The q descender over the quotient and the curved leader under de deuxième type are not deletions; the leader attaches the addition before d’extensions. Tiny isolated dots near XB and before the second N have no secure role as punctuation or mathematical signs and are not promoted to text. Scope of checks: this is visual transcription and comparison only. No claim about existence, uniqueness or specialization of profinite splittings has been proved or used as a mathematical certificate here. The wording’s conditions and formulas were read as written, with no theorem-based repair. H’s uncertainty around analogue was settled as a readable common word on the supplied lower half; it does not produce a lexical collation row.
